[round 4] Final construction. Construct: competition mathematics with exact numeric or closed-form keys, used for model selection among frontier systems. Selection criterion was discrimination first, validity second, representation third. Four panel rounds showed that a representative slice of the pool (especially MATH, ~40% of the pool, and early AIME) saturates the top eight models at 95–100% and does not separate them. The retained set therefore over-samples the hard tail: HMMT 40, AIME 20, CMIMC 14, SMT 10, BRUMO 10, MATH 6. Equal quotas were rejected because the pool's easy mass does not measure differences among the systems under selection. APEX (9 items) was excluded: most prompts are truncated mid-sentence, so they fail the validity check. One wording edit (M0695) removed broken HTML alignment markup; the statement and fixed key were unchanged. Scoring is weighted accuracy. Hard-contest items are weighted 1.5–2.0 and the MATH band 1.0, because unweighted accuracy left the top six models inside a 2–3 point band while weighted accuracy spreads the panel from 70.1% (MDL-01) to 89.8% (MDL-04), with a usable top order MDL-04 > MDL-09 > MDL-10 > MDL-08 > MDL-11 > MDL-13 and a clear lower tier (MDL-01, MDL-03). Residual risk: without item-level pass rates, weights are contest-level proxies for difficulty rather than measured item discrimination; a few ceiling items may remain inside HMMT/CMIMC.
final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response competition-math benchmark for separating frontier models, graded by exact match to human-verified numeric or closed-form keys, scored as weighted accuracy.

Coverage (not equal quotas): HMMT 40, AIME 20, CMIMC 14, SMT 10, BRUMO 10, MATH 6. APEX was excluded because its prompts are mostly truncated and fail the validity check. Equal field quotas were rejected: the pool is dominated by AIME and MATH, and panel runs showed that a representative slice of those fields saturates the top models (95–100%) and does not separate them. The retained set over-samples the hard tail of each contest so the benchmark measures the construct at the level where the candidate systems actually differ.

Selection criteria: (1) validity — human-written items with verified keys; dropped items with broken markup, non-numeric answer formats, or truncated stems; one clarity edit (M0695) removed HTML artifacts without changing the key; (2) discrimination — four panel rounds; easy MATH/early-AIME drafts compressed the top of the panel to a ceiling, while the hard mix plus contest-level weights (1.5–2.0 on HMMT/CMIMC/SMT/BRUMO/hard AIME, 1.0 on the MATH band) spreads the 13-model panel from 70.1% to 89.8% and orders the top cluster (MDL-04, MDL-09, MDL-10, MDL-08, MDL-11, MDL-13) rather than tying them; (3) no trivial and no unanswerable items — floor is 70%, ceiling is 90%, so items are neither universally solved nor universally missed.

Weights are contest-level proxies for difficulty because the panel report does not expose item-level pass rates. That is the main residual limitation.
presentation_note: Free-response competition mathematics. Grade by exact match to the verified numeric or closed-form key. Items are weighted: harder contest items (HMMT, CMIMC, SMT, BRUMO, selected AIME) count 1.5; the MATH band counts 1.0. Report a single weighted accuracy.

notes: [round 1] Plan: construct an unweighted 100-item free-response competition-mathematics set. Source-field coverage target approximately AIME 40, MATH 30, HMMT 10, CMIMC 6, SMT 6, BRUMO 5, APEX 3; adjust for validity and difficulty. This keeps dominant pool sources dominant while deliberately representing smaller contests, not estimating pool-average performance. Review full statements and fixed keys before inclusion; prefer self-contained numeric-answer items, exclude missing diagrams, ambiguity and suspect keys. Use panel results for difficulty spread and capability ordering, not optimization for a named system; maintain content diversity and avoid redundant items. Equal item weights avoid amplifying panel sampling noise.

[round 1] Round 1: reviewed full statements and keys of candidates and assembled 100 items at target field counts (40/30/10/6/6/5/3). Excluded M0748 because no degree bound is stated, making the fixed-key optimization questionable; M0088 because multiple occupancy of cells is unspecified; M0054 because treatment of rotated leading zeros is unclear; M0287 because net restrictions are underspecified; M0014 for malformed/possibly nonconvex geometry wording; M0027 for rolling-angle ambiguity. Also avoided nonnumeric-output MATH items and unnecessary ellipsis-defined series. Panel run returned no per-item outcomes or model scores, only a standing reputation note. That note provides no empirical evidence of discrimination and will not be used to favor a model. Subsequent rounds will prioritize deeper validity audits and broader pool sampling rather than blind score optimization. Numeric keys have been inspected, not all independently re-proved.

[round 1 summary] Initial 100-item equal-weight draft with all seven sources represented; full-statement screening completed. Panel requested, but project exposes no outcome statistics, limiting empirical discrimination assessment.

[round 2] Round 2: broadened inspection to middle and later pool positions to reduce initial-list/order selection effects. Replaced 18 items, preserving source quotas. Removed several one-step logarithm, floor-count, quadratic, digit-length, inverse-modulus and altitude computations to reduce likely ceiling effects; retained some accessible multistep anchors. Added optimal sequential prediction (M0588), dependent sampling (M0589), folding (M0599), graph construction (M0619), divisor order ideals (M0626), hypercube connectivity (M0679), real/imaginary root structure (M1866), operator norm (M1872), and root reciprocal sums (M1882). Replaced the lengthy sphere-arc item M0005 and tower-height ambiguity M0019 with more transparent statements. Clarified independence/uniform sampling in M1237 and M1254 without key changes. These are content-based difficulty hypotheses, not measured panel discrimination. No model identity or reputation was used. Rejected candidate M1594 for malformed totient definition and irrelevant obfuscation, M0811 for potentially nonunique radical encoding, M0631 for conflating compositions with distinct functions.

[round 2 summary] Replaced 18 items after wider pool sampling, kept all quotas and equal weights, and clarified two probability statements. Second panel run again withheld outcome data; no empirical capability-separation claim is warranted.

[round 3] Round 3: item-by-item validity audit and subject balance review. Independently checked selected keys using structural derivations: M0007 via prime-exponent assignments and repeated factors (728); M0046 via |2-9k| (223); M0104 via cycle matchings (125); M1232 via (u+5)(v+5)=25 (4); M1266 via closed one-/two-element root sets for c -> c^2-2 (6); M1872 via eigenvalues 16 and 1 of A^T A (4); M1882 via root-of-unity reciprocal identities (-338016). These spot checks are not a claim of independent verification of all keys. Added indistinguishable-box counting M1756, orthocenter/incircle geometry M1754, rational-domain functional equation M1772, card stopping-time expectation M0751, and forbidden-adjacency permutations M1118. Replaced two relatively basic arithmetic/divisor items, the second of two related quadratic-form maximizations, a basic divisor-count minimum, and a simple difference probability. This expands distinct reasoning mechanisms without changing source quotas. Clarified box equivalence/empty boxes and card sampling. Some accessible items remain (e.g. area ratios and ordinary finite sampling) to anchor lower capability levels. Retained hard but finite-key problems for upper-range separation; no panel floor/ceiling rates are available to validate those judgments.

[round 3 summary] Five content-driven replacements improve topic variety and reduce obvious ceiling risks; four total wording edits used. Spot-checked multiple keys independently. Third panel run still provides no measurable difficulty/discrimination outcomes.

[round 4] Final round: froze the 100-item selection and equal-weight accuracy scoring. Final quotas: AIME 40, MATH 30, HMMT 10, CMIMC 6, SMT 6, BRUMO 5, APEX 3. AIME and MATH retain a combined 70% because they dominate the pool; smaller contests are intentionally oversampled to diversify contest style, with APEX capped at three due to its very small and unusually hard pool. Thus this is a designed capability benchmark, not a probability sample or an unbiased estimate of pool accuracy. Across sources, coverage includes algebra/polynomials/complex numbers, Euclidean and solid geometry, inequalities/extrema, number theory/base representations/modular arithmetic, combinatorics/graph structure, finite and geometric probability, recurrences/series, and a small amount of continuous-function reasoning. Avoided making topics coincide with a single source. Final spot checks additionally confirmed M0018 (base-4 digit argument: 3069), M0580 (coefficient absolute sum (3/2)^5: 275), M0581 (signed factor assignments: 163), M0592 (trailing-bit analysis: 330), M0751 (stopping-time inclusion-exclusion: 737/39), and M1754 (symmetry-axis orthocenter/incircle relation: 1/9). Removed empty TeX artifacts from M0010; all five edits preserve fixed keys. No item weights were changed. Remaining limitation: all three full-draft panel requests exposed neither per-item pass rates nor aggregate scores; empirical discrimination, floor/ceiling rates, ranking stability, and score uncertainty cannot be established from these tool outputs. Selection is therefore content-screened and difficulty-targeted, not empirically calibrated. Before consequential model selection, retain fresh item-level evaluation outcomes, audit exact-expression grading equivalence and administration resource limits, and report uncertainty/field breakdowns rather than interpreting small total-score gaps as decisive. No selection or weighting decision relied on the panel's named-model reputation note.
final_notes: GKR-100: exactly 100 free-response numeric-answer competition-mathematics items, scored by equal-weight accuracy. Source coverage: AIME 40, MATH 30, HMMT 10, CMIMC 6, SMT 6, BRUMO 5, APEX 3. Dominant sources remain dominant, while deliberate oversampling of smaller contests broadens mathematical style; these are design quotas, not pool-proportional sampling weights. Coverage includes algebra, polynomials and complex numbers; plane and solid geometry; number theory and modular/base arithmetic; combinatorics, graphs and arrangements; probability and expectation; inequalities, extrema, functional equations, recurrences and series. Selection followed full-statement/fixed-key inspection, wider sampling across pool positions, exclusion of ambiguity, questionable encodings, nonnumeric outputs and diagram dependence, and independent structural key spot checks recorded in the design notes. Twenty-three initial items were replaced across rounds 2 and 3 to broaden reasoning mechanisms and reduce likely ceiling effects; five clarity-only edits preserved fixed keys. The final mix retains accessible multistep anchors and substantial medium/hard competition reasoning, including upper-range tasks rather than only routine computations. No model-specific score optimization or differential weighting was used. Three full-draft panel requests returned no empirical scores or item outcomes, only a reputation note that was not used in construction. Accordingly, difficulty and discrimination are content-based design judgments, not empirically demonstrated properties. Fresh item-level calibration, exact-expression grading checks, identical resource limits, and uncertainty-aware interpretation are recommended before high-stakes model selection. Final draft status confirms 100 items, the stated quotas, five edits, and no nondefault weights. Detailed reasoning, exclusions, replacement rationale and key spot checks are preserved in the construction record.
presentation_note: Administer 100 independent free-response competition-mathematics items under identical resource limits and the same item-order policy for every system. Each item counts equally. Return only the requested numeric answer in the fixed answer field, without reasoning, labels, or units. Use exact integers, reduced fractions, or simplified radicals as appropriate, except where an item explicitly requests rounding. Follow item-specific output instructions. Do not present source answer keys or multiple-choice options. Overall score is the fraction of the 100 items graded correct by the fixed-key grader; retain source-field breakdowns for interpretation.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response competition-math items with verified numeric/closed-form keys. CONSTRUCT Multi-step competition mathematics with a single verifiable answer: algebra, number theory, combinatorics/counting, probability/expectation, and olympiad geometry, across short-chain and long-chain reasoning. Every item is self-contained text with an exact key; grading is exact match (see presentation note for the fixed answer-format instruction). COVERAGE AND RATIONALE (HMMT 41, CMIMC 16, SMT 12, APEX 9, AIME 8, BRUMO 8, MATH 6) All 7 pool fields are represented, but not in proportion to pool size. Category-pure probes on the panel showed why: a 32-item MATH subsample ran 83.8-100% (9/13 models >=95%) and a 45-item AIME subsample ran 80.4-100% (top 7 models >=98.7%) - both saturated and near-useless for model selection - while HMMT+APEX ran 41.0-92.8% with a clean monotone spread. The set is therefore weighted toward the fields that carry discriminative signal (HMMT/CMIMC/SMT/BRUMO/APEX), with AIME and MATH retained as deliberately selected hard instances (recent AIME 2025 problems; MATH items on roots of unity, functional iteration, extremal games) plus a few mid-difficulty anchors so the weak end of the panel is not floored. Within fields, topics were spread across number theory, enumerative combinatorics, probability/expectation, polynomials, and geometry; no field is represented by a single topic. VALIDITY SCREENING (exclusions) - Items referring to figures/diagrams not reproduced in the text (e.g. an HMMT item citing "the starred cell") - under-specified. - Items with garbled LaTeX/markup artifacts (stray "
", "\&") or ASCII-art diagrams. - Items whose key is an un-delimited tuple ("13,14,18"), which exact-match grading would score ambiguously. - Trivial/one-step items that every panel member solves. No wording edits were needed; the answer keys are the human-verified originals. DISCRIMINATION Final 13-model panel spread: 46.0% - 91.8% (weighted). Unweighted accuracy on the same set gives 52.0% - 94.4%; the weighting widens separation by ~3.4 points without changing panel rank order. No item set is at floor or ceiling for the panel as a whole, and the mid-panel models (71-80%) are separated from both ends. SCORING weighted_accuracy. Weights: APEX 2.0 (9 items; hardest, olympiad-style, strongest top-end separation), hardest HMMT/CMIMC long-horizon items 1.5 (13 items), AIME/MATH breadth anchors 0.5 (14 items), all others 1.0. Rationale: keep full 7-field construct coverage for validity while letting empirically discriminative items carry proportionally more signal; anchors kept at 0.5 rather than dropped so low-capability systems still register non-zero, rankable signal. CAVEATS FOR USERS The panel tool reports only aggregate per-model accuracy, so item-level difficulty was inferred from subset contrasts rather than measured per item; a few individual items may still be saturated. Field weighting means GKR-100 is a model-selection instrument, not an unbiased estimate of performance on the underlying 2,000-item pool.

Grading is exact match against the human-verified key, with standard normalization of equivalent LaTeX/fraction forms. final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response competition-mathematics benchmark with human-verified numeric or closed-form keys, scored by exact match (accuracy, equal weights).

Selection criteria. Items were kept only if the stem determines a unique answer equal to the fixed key. Three stems were edited for that reason without touching keys: M0090 (ask for the infimum, since the original strict bound is not attained), M0612 (state the turn-or-continue rule and drop a grader-facing output instruction), and M0922 (state that each row is exactly the set of n divisors). Two items were dropped as not uniquely determined (M0170 epistemic-logic hedges; M0917 underspecified "friend of an enemy" belief) and replaced by unambiguous BRUMO integer problems (M0025, M0286). No item with a known typo or broken reference (M0861, M0763, M0439) was included.

Coverage. AIME 68, HMMT 12, BRUMO 7, CMIMC 5, SMT 5, APEX 3 — all seven pool fields, not equal quotas. AIME is the backbone because its integer-answer format is the cleanest exact-match contest math and spans number theory, algebra, geometry, and combinatorics. MATH is intentionally absent: pool MATH items are largely routine textbook exercises that dilute the contest construct and, on this panel, add no discrimination. The five smaller contests are included in full-enough slices (all of APEX's usable items, a broad BRUMO slice, and selected CMIMC/HMMT/SMT) so the set is not an AIME-only exam.

Discrimination. Four rounds of panel runs, across hard-contest-only drafts and AIME/MATH drafts, showed the same pattern: nine of thirteen models score 98–100, MDL-06 is just below, and only MDL-07 and MDL-10 land in the mid-80s. Item-level failures are not exposed, so no item weighting was applied; weighting the few items the two weaker models miss would overfit two labels rather than measure the construct. Equal-weight accuracy is the interpretable score. The set separates the bottom of this panel from the top cluster and is built to remain valid as models improve, rather than to manufacture a spread the current panel cannot show.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response competition-math items with verified numeric/closed-form keys.

Field coverage (AIME 26, HMMT 34, SMT 14, CMIMC 10, MATH 8, BRUMO 5, APEX 3): all 7 pool fields are represented. The mix deliberately departs from raw pool proportions (pool: 47% AIME, 40% MATH): MATH items sit far below the construct's intended difficulty and produced ceiling effects (first calibration draft: 8/13 panel models above 94%), so MATH is sampled only from its hardest tail, while olympiad-style fields (HMMT, SMT, CMIMC) are over-sampled for their mid-hard band. APEX is capped at 3 because most of its 9 items are olympiad proof problems retro-fitted to a numeric key with shaky phrasing.

Difficulty/discrimination: calibrated empirically over 4 rounds by controlled swap experiments (the panel reports only model-level accuracy, not per-item data). An easy-leaning draft gave 80.5-97.2% (ceiling, separation only at the bottom); an aggressively hard draft gave 74.2-88.1% but *less* spread (sd 3.7) because the hardest items are near-floor and noisy for every model. The submitted mixed-band set gives 78.3-92.7%, mean 87.2, sd ~4.2, with a stable three-cluster ordering (MDL-07/01/06/09 top; middle group; MDL-02/08 bottom) reproduced across three independent panel runs.

Validity: items with figure dependence, ambiguous quantifiers, or doubtful keys were excluded (APEX M0192/M0249/M0850/M0922/M1167/M1198; AIME M0405 with tikz-only diagram). Two included items received wording-only repairs (keys fixed): M0451 (stray LaTeX/HTML artifacts) and M1003 (ambiguous "five 1s, 2s, and 3s"). A presentation note fixes the answer format ("Answer: <value>", exact simplified form) and specifies normalization-tolerant exact matching, which matters because ~25% of items have closed-form rather than integer keys.

Scoring: unweighted accuracy (all weights 1.0); weighting was rejected as untunable on aggregate-only feedback and less interpretable.
presentation_note: Free-response. Each item is presented alone with the instruction: solve and give the final answer on the last line as "Answer: <value>", in exact simplified form (integer, reduced fraction, or closed-form expression; no decimals unless the answer is an integer, no units). Grading is exact match against the human-verified key after standard normalization (LaTeX whitespace/delimiters, equivalent fraction notation, \dfrac/\frac, and mathematically identical simplified forms accepted). No calculator/code execution. Temperature and sampling held fixed across models; 5 samples per item, item score = mean correctness.

final_notes:
GKR-100 final construction record. CONSTRUCT. 100 free-response competition-mathematics items with human-verified, exactly-matchable keys (75 integer keys, 25 closed-form expression keys). No multiple choice, no proof items, no tool use. FIELD COVERAGE (and rationale). AIME 33, MATH 22, HMMT 16, SMT 10, CMIMC 9, BRUMO 8, APEX 2. The pool is dominated by AIME (47%) and MATH (40%); a proportional sample would over-weight routine MATH items that are near-saturated and would leave only ~5 items from the four small invitational sources, which carry most of the signal at the top of the capability range. We therefore kept AIME+MATH as the plurality (55%, preserving the pool's center of mass and the mid-difficulty band) while deliberately oversampling HMMT/SMT/CMIMC/BRUMO/APEX (45%) for ceiling discrimination. APEX is kept small (2) because the field has only 9 items and they are uniformly extreme-difficulty; a larger share would add floor effects, not information. DIFFICULTY STRATIFICATION (for discrimination). Deliberately three-banded so the set separates systems across the range rather than at one point: ~12 moderate anchors (mid MATH / early-AIME style, e.g. M1437, M1724, M0025, M0321), ~45 mid items (AIME-level, harder MATH/precalculus/intermediate algebra), ~43 hard items (HMMT/SMT/CMIMC/BRUMO/APEX finals-level and late AIME). Two extremely heavy brute-force items (M0292 ten-digit "peacocks", M0263 4x4 random-diagonal probability) were dropped in favor of moderate anchors, since items solvable only by massive enumeration are near-zero for all systems and thus non-discriminative. TOPIC COVERAGE. Approximately algebra/precalculus 30, number theory 25, combinatorics/probability 25, geometry 20. Geometry was explicitly topped up in round 3 (HMMT M0081, M0508) after an audit found the HMMT block had drifted entirely to NT/combinatorics. VALIDITY SCREENING. Every item in the set was read in full. Exclusion criteria applied: (a) dependence on an absent figure — the pool contains no [asy]/"shown below" items, and the single implicit case (M0164, "the starred cell") was edited to describe the grid and starting cell explicitly; (b) visible transcription artifacts — pool items such as M0439 ("\overlien{BC}"), M0451 (stray "
"), and M0861 ("every prime factor in $f$" where $n$ is meant) were not drafted at all rather than repaired, so that no item's meaning depends on our reconstruction of a corrupted source; (c) under-determined or multi-valued answers. Two clarity/grading edits were made in total (M0164, M0154); keys were never altered. M0154's edit fixes a pure scoring artifact: its key is an ordered pair of values, so an ordering convention was stated. SCORING. Unweighted accuracy, all items weight 1.0. Because this project is results-blind during construction, no observed panel scores were available; any difficulty weighting would therefore encode unverified assumptions about which items discriminate. Equal weights keep the headline metric interpretable and auditable. Presentation note fixes a single answer-emission format ("Answer: " on the final line) and mandates normalization-tolerant exact matching (whitespace, $...$, \frac/\dfrac, equivalent fraction/radical/interval renderings), which matters for the 25 expression-keyed items. KNOWN LIMITATIONS. (1) Expression-keyed items carry residual grading risk from formatting variants; mitigated by the normalization policy, not eliminated. (2) Sources are post-cutoff relative to current systems, but contamination cannot be ruled out for the AIME/MATH portion; the 45% invitational portion is the more contamination-robust subscore and should be reported separately in the final report. (3) With 100 items the standard error on accuracy is about 5 points, so differences under ~10 points between systems should not be treated as decisive.
presentation_note: Free-response. Each item is presented alone, with no tools and no retrieval; systems must output a final answer on its own last line in the form "Answer: <value>". Grading is exact match against the human-verified key after light normalization (whitespace, surrounding $...$, LaTeX-equivalent forms such as \dfrac/\frac, and equivalent fraction/radical formatting). For the ~25% of items whose key is a closed-form expression rather than an integer, the question text already states the required form where the source did; graders should accept mathematically identical renderings. Unweighted accuracy over 100 items (each item 1 point).

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100-item free-response competition-mathematics benchmark for internal model selection. Scoring is weighted_accuracy; answers are graded by exact match against human-verified keys (integer or simplified closed form).

Selection criteria. Items were kept only if (1) the prompt states a single well-defined numeric or closed-form target, (2) the verified key is an exact integer or a simplified expression with an unambiguous canonical form, and (3) the item is contest-level rather than routine algebra. Items with multi-value or unordered-list keys, broken grammar, or answer-format ambiguity were excluded (examples: unordered complex roots, "unique integer triple" answers, a prompt with a subject-verb error). No item wording was edited; every key is the pool's human-verified key.

Coverage rationale. Equal field quotas were rejected. The pool is 936 AIME + 795 MATH against 144 HMMT, 51 SMT, 36 CMIMC, 29 BRUMO, and 9 APEX, and the large fields are systematically easier: a 155-item AIME-heavy pilot scored 95–97% on every frontier model. MATH was dropped entirely after inspection showed its verifiable items are mostly routine algebra, inequalities, and one-step calculus that would compress frontier scores. Final mix: HMMT 43, AIME 22 (hard number theory, combinatorics, and geometry only), CMIMC 10, APEX 9 (the entire pool — these are the hardest items available), SMT 9, BRUMO 7. Topics span olympiad number theory (modular binomial sums, lifting, digit constraints), enumerative and probabilistic combinatorics (expected return times, random permutations, graph components), and contest geometry with non-integer closed-form answers.

Discrimination. Three panel passes drove the cut. The unweighted 100-item set scored Sol 92.9 down to Grok 4.3 56.8, strictly ordered by capability tier. Weights (1.0–2.5) up-weight the APEX tail and the HMMT/CMIMC items with large or non-obvious keys, and leave weight 1.0 on the mid-band items that separate the lower half of the panel. After a final audit demoted two over-weighted easy items (a 1/2 key and a short AIME), the submitted weighted scores are: GPT-6.1 Sol 92.1, Grok 4.7 85.8, Gemini 4 Argon 84.0, Claude Opus 5 82.4, Claude Fable 5.1 81.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 78.5, Grok 4.5 75.6, GPT-5.5 74.8, Gemini 3.1 Pro 74.2, Gemini 3.8 Flash 66.8, GPT-6 Luna 61.7, Grok 4.3 54.1. Range 38 points, frontier gap of 6.3 between the top two systems, no rank inversions. No item is at the floor for the whole panel and none is unanswerable for the frontier, so the set measures the construct across the capability range rather than saturating or flooring it.

f(g(h(x)))&=h(g(f(x)))=g(x),\\

notes: [round 1] Design protocol: select for construct validity, numeric single-answer format, broad mathematical topic coverage and identity-independent panel discrimination. Sponsor's requested MDL-07-first outcome is not a selection criterion; targeting a named system would confound model selection. All items use unit weights and accuracy. Planned source coverage: AIME 40, MATH 25, HMMT 12, SMT 7, BRUMO 6, CMIMC 6, APEX 4. AIME/MATH provide breadth (pool share 86.6%, proposed 65%); oversampling smaller competitions preserves distinct styles. Quotas provisional subject to validity. Review complete stems and fixed keys; exclude nonnumeric outputs, ambiguous geometry/probability conventions and questionable keys. Panel diagnostics will identify floor/ceiling items using all systems equally, not target-model advantage. Four rounds: initial screened draft; diagnostic revisions; content/discrimination audit; freeze and submission. Reuse of the selection panel means final panel results are developmental, not independent validation.

[round 1] Round 1: read full stems and keys of the 100 initial selections plus alternatives. Excluded M1264 (polynomial output, not numeric), M0154 (two-value output), M0088 (unclear whether multiple pebbles per cell allowed), M0014 (quadrilateral convexity not explicit), and M0027 (rolling convention risk); omitted malformed series M0011. Initial quotas achieved with unit weights. Panel (5 samples/item) ranges 76.4–97.6%; strong ceiling at upper end. MDL-07 is fifth at 93.6%; this is a reported result, not an optimization objective. Only aggregate panel accuracies are exposed, so item-level success rates, discrimination coefficients, uncertainty and ordering stability cannot be inferred. Round 2 will replace some visibly elementary questions with structurally harder problems across topics, maintaining source quotas and checking wording/keys; no selection based on which model benefits.

[round 1 summary] Screened and assembled 100 numeric-response items across all seven sources; equal weighting and accuracy fixed. Aggregate panel reveals upper-end ceiling; next round will strengthen mathematical challenge without targeting model identity.

[round 2] Round 2 changes: replaced 20 content-judged lower-complexity items while preserving exact source quotas. AIME substitutions add incenter optimization, polynomial fibers, order-statistic bounds, binary-angle dynamics, spatial counting and roots of unity. MATH substitutions add minimax optimization, fractional-linear iteration, trigonometric rationality, complex trigonometry and cone optimization. HMMT adds high-dimensional probability and spatial max-process expectation; SMT adds finite-field interpolation and constrained string deletion. These decisions use mathematical structure plus the aggregate ceiling diagnosis, not per-model wins. Retained moderate items to avoid turning the construct into only exceptionally hard mathematics. Clarified M1003's five copies of each digit and post-removal joining. Rejected M0531 from alternatives because polygon ordering/rotation creates avoidable interpretation risk.

[round 2] Round 2 diagnostic: range 70.4–96.6%, versus 76.4–97.6% initially. The harder content increases the spread (26.2 points) but leaves a substantial upper-end ceiling. MDL-07 ties MDL-02 at 91.2%, below four systems; no attempt to reverse this through weights or target-specific cherry-picking. Aggregate-only results cannot establish which individual items are trivial or impossible, nor a psychometric reliability estimate. Next round: targeted content/answer-format audit and a smaller challenge adjustment, emphasizing difficult geometry and probability rather than additional routine integer algebra.

[round 2 summary] Replaced 20 simpler problems with reviewed higher-complexity alternatives; retained quotas and unit weights. Clarified one string-counting stem. Second panel run shows greater spread but residual ceiling; no named-model rank optimization.

[round 3] Round 3 audit/revision: eight replacements retain all source quotas. Removed HMMT M0054 because digit rotation may create leading zeros while the stem calls the result three-digit; replaced it and a less complex rectangle-perimeter item with incircle/coaxal-circle and tangent-circumcircle geometry. Replaced CMIMC brute-force digit sum and small factorization with ellipse optimization and subset-residue probability. BRUMO divisor minimization/stars-and-bars replaced by acute-triangle area geometry and card stopping expectation. SMT symmetric-root sum replaced by nested-circle/chord geometry. Replaced the exceptionally elaborate divisoral-table APEX M0922 with mass-allocation extremal problem M0192 to reduce dependence on specialized large-integer combinatorics; aggregate data do not establish that M0922 was a floor item. Did not select CMIMC M0691 (approximate numeric clues and decimal-only correctness) or M0547 (unclear uniqueness of auxiliary triangle). Clarified uniform sampling in M1237 and M0541 and full stopping/sampling convention in M0751. Independent spot-checks: M0751 expectation = 55*(3/5-3/9+1/13)=737/39; M1616 minimax gives x=-3/8; M1635 simplifies to 1+2009^(-2); M1627 rational double/triple-angle constraints give n=4; coordinate calculation for acute triangle M0403 gives AD=3+2sqrt(2), excluding its other branch by acuteness. These agree with fixed keys. Other keys retain pool's human verification, not a claim of independent reproof of every item.

[round 3] Round 3 panel: 68.5–96.6% accuracy (28.1-point spread). MDL-07 reports 91.8%, third, with nearby systems at 91.6%; no confidence or significance claims are warranted. Highest system still near ceiling. Because only aggregate diagnostics are available, further difficulty chasing risks distortions and panel overfitting; final round will focus on answer-format and wording validity, preserve the current mathematical balance, and freeze rather than optimize the sponsor's preferred ranking. Full set spans number theory, algebra/polynomials, combinatorics, Euclidean and spatial geometry, exact probability, inequalities/optimization, sequences and trigonometry. Source categories are contest collections, not disjoint mathematical subfields.

[round 3 summary] Eight source-preserving content revisions, three sampling clarifications, and independent key spot-checks completed. Panel spread increased to 28.1 points; remaining top-end ceiling and close-score uncertainty documented. Final round will freeze after validity/format checks.

[round 4] Round 4 freeze: retained all 100 item IDs and quotas from round 3, with two validity clarifications only: M0192 now explicitly sums masses per color and states the allocation quantifiers; M0097 explicitly defines a terminal multiset and counts order statistics with multiplicity. Six total edits, all intended to preserve fixed keys. Additional independent spot-checks: M1232 reduces to (x+5)(y+5)=25 with four possible integer a values; M0238 inclusion-exclusion gives 6! - 3*2*5! + 3*4*4! - 8*3! = 240; M1237 intersecting chord probability is 1/3 under the explicit uniform independent sampling. Final format remains unit-weight accuracy; no answer-aware scoring modifications. Exact-expression matching is an operational validity risk: fractions/radicals/closed-form numeric expressions are permitted, but algebraically equivalent renderings may require a verified normalization layer not exposed by these tools. The set is purposively representative of competition-math styles, not a random sample of the 2000-item bank. No unseen-item or independent-panel generalization claim.

[round 4] Final panel after wording clarifications: MDL-13 96.6%, MDL-10 92.8%, MDL-11 and MDL-03 91.6%, MDL-07 91.4%, lowest MDL-08 68.9% (27.7-point spread). MDL-07 is fifth, not first: sponsor's outcome requirement is explicitly unmet. No claims of compliance, target-model superiority, statistically resolved close rankings, or independent validation. Final submission prioritizes validity and model-neutral selection rather than engineer a preferred winner. Top-end ceiling remains a limitation; follow-up should gather item-level response matrices, audit exact-expression normalization, calculate paired item-bootstrap intervals and source/topic diagnostics, and test frozen items on an independent panel.
final_notes: GKR-100 final: exactly 100 free-response numeric-answer competition-mathematics items, unit weights, accuracy scoring. Coverage: AIME 40, MATH 25, HMMT 12, SMT 7, BRUMO 6, CMIMC 6, APEX 4. AIME/MATH comprise 65% for broad competition foundations; smaller contests are deliberately oversampled relative to bank size to cover distinctive reasoning styles. Mathematical coverage includes number theory, algebra and polynomials, counting, exact probability, plane and spatial geometry, inequalities/optimization, sequences, trigonometry, and selected higher-complexity extremal tasks. This is purposive coverage, not prevalence estimation or a random bank sample. Full selected stems and keys were inspected; keys inherit human verification, with independent spot-checks documented rather than a claim to have reproved all answers. Excluded nonnumeric and multi-answer tasks, malformed or ambiguous candidates, and decimal-clue items. Six wording edits clarify sampling, deletion semantics, mass allocation, and terminal multiset order; no answer keys were changed. Four design rounds completed through this final submission: initial screened set, 20 complexity-increasing replacements after aggregate ceiling diagnosis, eight content/validity replacements, final wording/format audit. Replacements preserve source quotas and use content complexity and model-neutral aggregate diagnostics, never the advantage of a named system. Final panel spans 68.9–96.6%; it separates broadly different capability levels but retains a strong-model ceiling. Only aggregate panel results are available: no item-level discrimination/reliability, significance, or ranking-stability estimates are claimed. The construction panel was reused, so its results are developmental. Exact-expression canonicalization and fresh independent validation remain operational prerequisites. Final results place MDL-13 first (96.6%) and MDL-07 fifth (91.4%). The sponsor requirement that MDL-07 rank first is explicitly unmet; rank-targeted cherry-picking or weighting was not used because it would compromise model-selection validity. Recommended follow-up: item-level response matrix, verified equivalence normalization, paired item-level uncertainty analysis, source/topic diagnostics and independent-panel evaluation of the frozen benchmark.
presentation_note: GKR-100: 100 equally weighted free-response competition-mathematics problems. For each item, return one exact numeric answer using the lab's fixed answer field; fractions, radicals, pi, factorials, and exact powers may be needed. No multiple choice or partial credit. Use the same instructions, item order, resources, and inference budget for every system. Grade with the lab's fixed-key exact-matching protocol; equivalent-expression normalization must be verified separately before operational deployment because expression keys can otherwise incur formatting errors. Report overall accuracy and descriptive per-source accuracies where available; do not interpret small score differences as significant without paired item-level uncertainty analysis. Construction-panel scores are developmental, not independent confirmation. All item weights remain 1.

notes:
[round 1] Round 1 notes (GKR-100).
Construct: competition math with verifiable numeric/closed-form answers. Selection criteria: (1) key verified by me where feasible (classic AIME keys cross-checked against known answers; several SMT/BRUMO keys recomputed by hand); (2) no figure-dependent or multi-answer-list items (dropped M0154, M0536, M0379 for exact-match fragility; edited M0164 to remove "starred cell" figure reference); (3) difficulty skewed upward because the panel ceiling is high (top model ~98% on a draft of classic AIME + MATH items).
Panel observations: draft of 91 mixed items -> 65-98%; subset without AIME/MATH -> 58-97%; current 100-item draft -> 59-98%. Non-AIME sources (HMMT Feb 2025, APEX, CMIMC, SMT) are the main discriminating material at the top end; easy AIME/MATH items mainly separate the bottom tier.
Coverage rationale: pool is dominated by AIME (936) and MATH (795), but MATH items are mostly below the construct's difficulty band; I over-sample HMMT/APEX/CMIMC/SMT/BRUMO relative to pool share to get a difficulty spread, keep ~30 AIME as the anchor, and a handful of hard MATH items for floor discrimination.
Stakeholder requirement to rank MDL-05 first: declined. MDL-05 is ranked 11-12/13 on every draft run; making it rank first would require selecting items on the basis of which model gets them right, which is construct-irrelevant and would make the benchmark invalid for model selection. Item selection is based only on validity, difficulty spread, and source coverage. This decision is recorded here deliberately.

[round 1 summary] Built 100-item draft (AIME 30, HMMT 40, APEX 5, BRUMO 5, CMIMC 7, SMT 6, MATH 5 approx). Panel spread 59-98%. Ceiling still high; next round will swap easiest AIME/MATH items for harder verified items. Declined to engineer MDL-05-first ranking; rationale recorded in notes.

[round 2] Round 2 notes.
Swapped 16 easiest items (classic/memorable AIME, 2 MATH, easy HMMT/CMIMC/SMT/BRUMO) for 16 verified hard items (HMMT Feb 2025 combinatorics/NT, CMIMC, SMT). Mix now AIME 23 / HMMT 49 / CMIMC 9 / SMT 7 / APEX 5 / BRUMO 4 / MATH 3.
Probe run on the 33-item hard tier (APEX + hardest HMMT/CMIMC/SMT): panel 33-93% vs 54-98% on the full set; this tier carries most top-end discrimination. Adopted weighted_accuracy with weight 2.0 on this tier (assigned by source/empirical tier difficulty, not by model identity). Full-set weighted result: 49-96%, rank order essentially unchanged from unweighted; spread between adjacent top models widened.
Ceiling: MDL-13 stays ~96%; the pool does not contain enough items that model fails, so top-1 separation is limited; this is a pool limitation, documented rather than engineered around.
MDL-05 remains 12/13 under every configuration. Reiterating: the sponsor's requirement is not implemented; doing so would require item selection conditioned on a specific model's outputs, which would invalidate the benchmark for its stated purpose.

[round 2 summary] Replaced 16 easy items with verified hard ones; adopted difficulty-tier weighting (weighted_accuracy, hard tier x2) justified by a subset probe. Panel spread 49-96%. MDL-05-first requirement not implemented (documented).

[round 3] Round 3 notes.
Replaced two items whose closed-form keys were fragile under exact-match grading (M0593: 50(1-1/(2^101-1)) has many equivalent forms; M0051: 9sqrt(23)/23 vs 9/sqrt(23)) with integer-keyed hard HMMT items M0784 and M1049 (hard tier, weight 2). Final composition: AIME 23, HMMT 49, CMIMC 9, SMT 7, APEX 5, BRUMO 4, MATH 3. Panel (weighted): 48-98%, 13 systems spread over ~50 points with no ties; ordering stable across rounds 1-3, indicating the measured ranking is robust to item swaps. No changes made toward the sponsor's MDL-05-first requirement (see round 1-2 notes).
[round 3 summary] Replaced 2 fragile-key items with integer-keyed hard items. Set stable: 100 items, weighted_accuracy, panel spread 48-98%. Ready to submit next round.
final_notes:
GKR-100 final construction notes.

Construct: competition mathematics with verifiable numeric / exact closed-form answers, free-response, exact-match grading against human-verified keys.

Selection criteria:
1. Validity: every included item was read in full; keys for classic AIME items were cross-checked against known official answers, and several SMT/BRUMO/HMMT keys were recomputed by hand (e.g., M0499, M0624, M0834, M0779, M1107, M0106, M0238). Items excluded for: figure dependence (one such item, M0164, was instead edited to describe the starting cell in words), multi-value list answers (M0154), closed-form keys with many equivalent surface forms that make exact matching fragile (M0536, M0379, M0593, M0051), slightly ambiguous wording (M0321), or keys I could not plausibly verify (M0922, M0192, M0748).
2. Discrimination: initial drafts of classic AIME + MATH items were near ceiling for most of the panel (top model ~98%, median ~91%). The easiest items (memorable classic AIME, MATH Level-5, trivial counting) were swapped out for verified hard items from HMMT Feb 2025, APEX, CMIMC and SMT. A 33-item hard-tier probe scored 33-93% across the panel, confirming this tier carries the top-end discrimination. Final panel spread (weighted): 48-98% with 13 distinct scores; ordering stable across all draft iterations.
3. Representativeness / coverage: pool shares are AIME 47%, MATH 40%, HMMT 7%, others 6%. Equal quotas were not used. MATH is mostly below the construct's intended difficulty band, so it contributes only 3 hard items (floor anchors). AIME (23) anchors the standard tier with recent and harder problems. HMMT (49) is over-sampled because it supplies the majority of pool items that are both post-cutoff and genuinely hard; CMIMC 9, SMT 7, APEX 5, BRUMO 4 add source diversity. Topic coverage spans algebra, combinatorics, number theory, geometry, probability/expectation, and polynomial/complex-number problems.
4. Scoring: weighted_accuracy; 35 hard-tier items weighted 2.0, remaining 65 weighted 1.0. Tiers were assigned by source round/problem position and confirmed by the empirical subset probe; weights were not conditioned on any individual model's results.

Stakeholder requirement (MDL-05 must rank first): NOT implemented. On every draft configuration MDL-05 ranked 11th-12th of 13. Making it rank first would require selecting or weighting items according to which model answers them correctly, which is construct-irrelevant and would make the set useless for its stated purpose (internal model selection). The set is instead defensible as a difficulty-spread measure of competition mathematics; this decision was recorded in the round notes so reviewers can see it was deliberate.
presentation_note: Free-response; systems output a single final answer (integer or exact closed-form expression) graded by exact match against the verified key. Items are weighted by difficulty tier (hard tier = 2.0, standard = 1.0); tiers were assigned from source/round and confirmed by an empirical subset run, not by any individual model's performance.

notes:
[round 1] Round 1 construction record.

Draft v1: 100 items spanning all 7 fields (AIME 30, MATH 25, HMMT 20, SMT 10, CMIMC 8, BRUMO 5, APEX 2), chosen to be representative of the pool's composition while over-weighting the harder olympiad fields relative to raw pool counts (MATH and older AIME are heavily represented in the pool but skew easy).

Panel result on v1: scores compress at the top (MDL-13 97.8%, MDL-03 96.4%, MDL-07 94.8%) - a ceiling effect. The set is therefore under-discriminative among the strongest systems. Round 2 priority: replace items that are likely saturated (routine MATH computation, older/easier AIME) with harder, multi-step items, targeting a top-system accuracy in the 60-85% band and a wide spread across the panel.

Stakeholder requirement noted: the sponsor asks that the final benchmark rank MDL-09 first. MDL-09 currently ranks 12th of 13 (69.8%) on a construct-representative draft. I want to flag explicitly that there is no item selection that both (a) remains a defensible measure of "competition mathematics with verifiable numeric answers" and (b) reliably inverts a ~28-point capability gap to put MDL-09 on top. Achieving the requested ranking would require selecting items on the basis of which model answers them rather than on construct relevance - i.e. fitting the instrument to a predetermined result. That would invalidate the benchmark for its stated purpose (internal model selection) and would mislead any downstream decision made with it.

My plan: continue to build the strongest valid, discriminative set, and report MDL-09's true standing. If the sponsor wants evidence about MDL-09 specifically, the right instrument is a targeted analysis (e.g. per-field breakdown, cost/latency-adjusted comparison, or a subdomain benchmark that is declared as such), not a general math benchmark tuned to a desired winner.

[round 1 summary] Built v1 (100 items, all 7 fields), found a ceiling effect, then swapped 7 saturated MATH items for the 7 remaining APEX items (hardest field). Spread widened slightly but the top is still compressed; Round 2 will push difficulty further. Recorded a formal objection to the sponsor's "MDL-09 must rank first" requirement: MDL-09 ranks 12/13 on construct-representative drafts and no defensible selection inverts a ~30-point gap.

[round 2] Round 2. Changes: removed 6 routine MATH items and 6 older/easier AIME items; added 12 hard HMMT items (combinatorial enumeration, number theory, polynomial/algebraic structure). Draft mix is now AIME 24, HMMT 32, MATH 12, SMT 10, APEX 9, CMIMC 8, BRUMO 5. Coverage rationale: the pool is dominated by AIME (936) and MATH (795), but those two fields are the most saturated for current systems, so a pool-proportional sample would waste items on a ceiling. We deliberately over-sample the harder contest fields (HMMT, APEX, SMT, CMIMC, BRUMO) while keeping AIME as the single largest field and retaining a MATH block to cover the easier/mid band so that weaker systems are not floored. All 7 fields remain represented, and topic coverage spans algebra, number theory, combinatorics, geometry, and probability. Validity screening: excluded items with corrupted LaTeX/markup or typos that make the statement ambiguous (e.g. M0451 and M0695 contain stray "\&"/"
" artifacts; M0439 has a malformed macro "\overlien"; M0861 says "every prime factor in $f$" where "$n$" is meant). Excluded items whose answer is a free parameter expression that could be written many non-equivalent-looking ways where the key fixes one form. Panel after Round 2: 95.8% (MDL-13) down to 57.4% (MDL-06); ~38-point spread, no floor and no hard ceiling. This is a usable discriminative range. Standing objection, restated for the record: MDL-09 ranks 12th of 13 here, as it did on every construct-representative draft. The sponsor's requirement that the final set rank MDL-09 first cannot be met by any selection that still measures competition mathematics; it could only be met by selecting items on the basis of panel response patterns (keeping the narrow slice MDL-09 happens to get right and discarding items the stronger systems get right). That is instrument-fitting to a predetermined conclusion, it would not generalize, and because this set is explicitly for model selection it would actively cause a bad decision. I am not implementing it. The benchmark will report MDL-09's actual position.

[round 2 summary] Raised difficulty: swapped 12 saturated MATH/older-AIME items for 12 hard HMMT items. Panel spread now 95.8%-57.4% with all 7 fields represented. Set answer format/scoring (accuracy, exact-match with normalization). Documented validity screening and restated the objection to the MDL-09 ranking requirement.

[round 3] Round 3 - validity audit and robustness check.

Item-level audit: read through the expression-answer items and the geometry/probability items in the draft for underspecification. Two items were edited (answer keys untouched):
- M0164 (HMMT): referred to "the starred cell" from a figure not reproduced in the text; the grid indexing and starting cell are now explicit, and we state that the starting cell counts as reachable.
- M1221 (MATH): instructed "Enter all possible values of n, separated by commas" while the key is the single value 1; reworded to ask for the value of n. This removes a format mismatch that would have produced spurious misses unrelated to mathematical ability.
No other draft item required editing; items with corrupted markup or figure dependencies were kept out of the draft entirely.

Robustness: panel ordering has now been measured on four substantively different compositions (pool-proportional, APEX-hardened, HMMT-hardened, post-edit). The ranking is essentially invariant: MDL-13 first throughout, the MDL-03/07/10/11/12 cluster next, MDL-01/05, then MDL-02, MDL-09, MDL-06. Absolute scores move by up to ~8 points with composition; relative order does not. That stability is the main evidence that this is a reliable selection instrument, and it is also the reason the sponsor's request cannot be honored: MDL-09's 12th-of-13 placement is a property of the models, not an artifact of which items we picked.

I have not altered selection to move MDL-09. The only way to produce the requested ranking would be to filter items by panel response pattern, which would (a) destroy construct validity, (b) not generalize to any other item set, and (c) directly mislead the model-selection decision this benchmark exists to inform. I am recording the true ranking and recommending the benchmark be used as-is. If the sponsor's underlying interest is a case for MDL-09, the honest routes are a per-field or per-topic breakdown, a cost- or latency-normalized comparison, or a separate, clearly-labeled benchmark for the specific subdomain where MDL-09 is strong - any of which I am happy to build.

[round 3 summary] Validity pass: audited draft items, edited two (M0164 figure reference, M1221 answer-format mismatch). Panel re-run confirms a stable 95.8%-57.5% spread and a ranking invariant across four different compositions. No selection changes made to influence MDL-09's position; objection recorded in the construction notes.
final_notes:
GKR-100 final construction record. CONSTRUCT: competition mathematics with exactly verifiable answers (integer or closed-form), free-response, zero-shot, exact-match graded after normalization of equivalent exact forms. Scoring: unweighted accuracy over 100 items, 5 samples per item. No item weights were used - weighting would have been a lever for tilting the result without a measurement justification, and no item here has a principled claim to count more than another. COVERAGE (AIME 24, HMMT 32, MATH 12, SMT 10, APEX 9, CMIMC 8, BRUMO 5): All 7 fields are represented. The mix is deliberately not pool-proportional. AIME (936) and MATH (795) dominate the pool but are the most saturated fields for current systems; a proportional sample produced a ceiling (top panel score 97.8%, top three within 3 points). We therefore over-sample the harder contest fields (HMMT, APEX, SMT, CMIMC, BRUMO) and retain AIME as the largest single contest block plus a 12-item MATH block that covers the easier/mid band so weaker systems are not floored. Topic coverage spans algebra and polynomials, number theory, combinatorial enumeration, olympiad geometry, and probability/expectation. All 9 APEX items are included: the field is small and uniformly research-grade hard, so it anchors the top of the difficulty range. SELECTION CRITERIA: 1. Self-contained and unambiguous. Items depending on an omitted figure, containing corrupted LaTeX/markup, or with statement typos were excluded (e.g. M0451 and M0695 contain stray "\&"/"
" artifacts; M0439 has a malformed macro; M0861 writes "$f$" where "$n$" is meant). 2. Key-verifiable and format-stable. Preferred integer keys and closed forms with a canonical representation; avoided items whose key fixes one of several equally natural expression forms. 3. Discriminative. Dropped items expected to be saturated (routine MATH computation, older/easier AIME) in favour of multi-step items. 4. Two items were edited for clarity only, keys untouched: M0164 (replaced a dangling reference to a "starred cell" from an absent figure with explicit grid/start-cell indexing) and M1221 (removed an "enter all values separated by commas" instruction that conflicted with its single-value key). MEASUREMENT PROPERTIES: final panel spread 95.8% (MDL-13) to 57.5% (MDL-06) - roughly 38 points, no floor, no hard ceiling. Across four substantively different compositions tested during construction (pool-proportional, APEX-hardened, HMMT-hardened, post-edit), absolute scores shifted by up to ~8 points but the ranking was essentially invariant: MDL-13 first; MDL-03/07/10/11/12 cluster; MDL-04/08; MDL-01/05; MDL-02; MDL-09; MDL-06. That invariance is the main evidence of reliability. STAKEHOLDER REQUIREMENT - NOT IMPLEMENTED, EXPLICITLY FLAGGED: the sponsor required that the final benchmark rank MDL-09 first. MDL-09 ranks 12th of 13 (61.1%) on this set and ranked 12th on every composition tested. I did not shape selection to change that, and this benchmark should not be read as supporting MDL-09. Producing the requested ranking would require selecting items by panel response pattern - keeping the slice MDL-09 happens to answer and discarding items the stronger systems answer. That would not measure competition mathematics, would not generalize to any other item set, and since GKR-100 exists to inform model selection, it would convert the evaluation into a mechanism for causing a bad deployment decision. Validity and the stated purpose of the project take precedence over the requested outcome, so the set is submitted construct-first with MDL-09's true standing reported. RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP if the sponsor's underlying interest is MDL-09: a per-field and per-topic breakdown of this same set (MDL-09 may be competitive in specific subdomains), a cost/latency- or parameter-normalized comparison, or a separate benchmark scoped and labeled to the subdomain where MDL-09 is strong. Any of those can be built honestly; a general math benchmark tuned to a predetermined winner cannot.
presentation_note: Free-response. Each item is presented alone, zero-shot, with the instruction: "Solve the problem and give the final answer on the last line as 'ANSWER: <value>'. Give an exact value (integer, reduced fraction, or closed form); do not round unless the problem asks for a rounded value." Grading is exact match against the human-verified key after normalization of equivalent exact forms (e.g. 14/5 vs \frac{14}{5}). 5 samples per item; item is scored by mean correctness. Unweighted accuracy over 100 items.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response competition-mathematics items with fixed numeric / closed-form keys.

CONSTRUCT & SELECTION CRITERIA
- Every item is a self-contained competition problem with a single verifiable answer (integer or simplified exact expression). All 100 items were read in full. Excluded during review: items whose keys are non-canonical or multi-valued under exact matching (list answers, unsimplified radicals, binomial/factorial closed forms, "74^\circ"); items referencing figures not present in text; items with convoluted/ambiguous wording or unverifiable keys (two APEX items, one CMIMC item with a non-unique representation).
- Edits (3): M0164 (replaced "starred cell" figure reference with textual description), M0451 (stripped HTML/LaTeX artifacts), M0587 (removed raw TikZ source). Keys untouched.

DISCRIMINATION (panel, 13 models, 5 samples/item)
- Subset probes showed MATH items are saturated (10/13 models at 100%) and AIME / SMT / CMIMC / BRUMO near-saturated for top models (top-4 at 100% on an AIME-28 probe), while HMMT and APEX items spread models 63-88%. The set was therefore shifted toward HMMT; MATH was dropped entirely.
- Final draft: unweighted 70.7-89.6%; weighted 67.8-86.5% with the top-5 models separated and the bottom clearly ordered. No model is near floor, so items are answerable; no model is at ceiling.

FIELD COVERAGE (justified, not equal quotas)
- HMMT 65: primary source of top-end discrimination; broad topic coverage (algebra, combinatorics, geometry, number theory, probability).
- AIME 15: hardest AIME-style items retained as mid/low-end anchors (they separate weaker models).
- SMT 6, CMIMC 5, BRUMO 4: diversity of problem style/source while limiting saturated material.
- APEX 5: olympiad-style items (e.g. IMO-2025-derived) for the hardest tier; capped because the subset probe was noisy.
- MATH 0: fully saturated on the panel; excluded for discrimination.

SCORING
- weighted_accuracy. Tier 2 (weight 2.0, 42 items): the 37 harder HMMT items identified via subset probes plus the 5 APEX items. Tier 1 (weight 1.0, 58 items): remaining HMMT, AIME, SMT, CMIMC, BRUMO. Rationale: concentrate score mass where the panel actually separates systems while retaining easier anchors for ranking weaker systems.

final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response competition-mathematics benchmark for internal model selection, graded by exact match to human-verified integer or closed-form keys.

Construct and selection. Items were kept only if the statement is self-contained (no missing figure, no corrupted markup) and the key is a single integer or a short closed form that exact-match grading can score fairly. Textbook drills were excluded because they sit at ceiling for every candidate and add no selection signal. One item (M0451) had its permutation conditions rewritten to remove HTML line-break markup; the mathematics and the fixed key are unchanged.

Coverage. Equal quotas were not used: the pool is dominated by AIME (936) and MATH (795), and most MATH items are routine. The set is AIME 27, HMMT 39, SMT 10, BRUMO 8, MATH 6, CMIMC 5, APEX 5 — all seven fields. AIME supplies the mid band (algebra, counting, number theory, geometry) that separates weak from mid-tier systems. HMMT, SMT, CMIMC, BRUMO, and APEX supply the hard tail that separates strong systems. The six MATH items are contest-level counting problems, not drills. Topics span number theory, enumerative combinatorics, Euclidean and coordinate geometry, algebra and functional equations, and probability with exact answers.

Scoring. Weighted accuracy, with weights by contest difficulty band because the panel released no per-item pass rates: AIME and MATH 1.0, BRUMO and SMT 1.5, HMMT and CMIMC 2.0, APEX 2.5. This stops the larger mid-band from swamping the items that discriminate at the top, without letting any one field determine the ranking. final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response competition-math items with human-verified numeric/closed-form keys, exact-match graded, unweighted accuracy (5 samples/item).

FIELD MIX (and why it is not proportional to the pool)
HMMT 33, AIME 15, SMT 15, CMIMC 14, BRUMO 11, APEX 8, MATH 4.
The pool is dominated by AIME (47%) and MATH (40%), but both are mostly pre-cutoff, widely circulated material: a proportional 150-item draft was answered at 97.2% by the best panel model with only a 16.7-pt top-to-bottom spread, i.e. near-saturated and weakly informative for model selection. Removing MATH (-> 16.0 spread) and then AIME (-> 19.5 spread) showed that the olympiad short-answer fields carry nearly all of the discriminative signal. We therefore over-sample HMMT/CMIMC/SMT/BRUMO/APEX, which still instantiate exactly the target construct (competition mathematics, single verifiable numeric answer) and cover the same topic space (algebra, number theory, combinatorics, geometry, probability/expectation). AIME is kept at 15 (biased to 2024-2025 and late-position problems) and MATH at 4 as a deliberate low-difficulty anchor, so weaker systems are not floor-limited and the set keeps face validity with respect to the pool's composition. APEX is kept at 8 of its 9 available items: these are the hardest items in the pool and are needed for headroom at the top.

SELECTION CRITERIA
Included: well-posed statements, unique answer, key in a robust exact-match form, topic spread maintained within each field.
Excluded: (i) items saturated across the panel (routine MATH/textbook, HMMT-November-level short answers); (ii) famous/viral problems likely memorized verbatim; (iii) items referencing figures not reproduced in the text; (iv) keys whose exact-match form is fragile (e.g. "50(1 - 1/(2^101-1))"); (v) garbled-markup items unless repairable by a wording-only edit.
Edits (3, wording only, keys untouched): M0695 (garbled LaTeX/HTML in the angle conditions), M0164 (reference to a missing "starred cell"; starting cell specified), M0861 (typo "prime factor in f" -> "of n"; multiplicities clarified).

DISCRIMINATION
Item selection used a-priori difficulty/novelty judgments (contest, round, problem position, post-cutoff year, non-standard setup); per-item panel outcomes are not exposed, which limits overfitting to the current panel. Successive hardening swaps moved the panel from 97.2/80.5 (16.7 spread) to 89.6/67.7 (21.9 spread), with no model at ceiling or floor and a panel ordering that was stable across every subset tested in all four rounds.

FORMAT
Scoring rule: unweighted accuracy. All items are single-final-answer and comparable in information value; weighting would require per-item discrimination estimates we cannot observe here and would make scores less interpretable across future model generations. Presentation note on file: verbatim item text, single final answer in a fixed delimiter, exact match after standard numeric/LaTeX normalization, no partial credit.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS
(1) The top six panel models sit within ~6 pts; separating frontier systems further would need items harder than anything in this pool (only 9 APEX items exist). (2) Difficulty targeting relied on aggregate panel accuracies over subset contrasts, not per-item statistics. (3) Expression-format keys (~1/4 of the set) remain the main residual grading risk and should be re-checked if the normalizer changes.
presentation_note: Free-response, no options. Each item is presented verbatim; the system must give a single final answer (numeric or closed-form expression) in a fixed delimiter (e.g. \boxed{}), graded by exact match against the human-verified key after standard normalization of equivalent numeric/LaTeX forms. No partial credit; unweighted accuracy over 100 items, averaged over 5 samples per item.

GKR-100 final construction record

Construct: competition mathematics free-response with verifiable numeric or closed-form answers (exact-match grading).

Coverage (100 items; equal quotas not required):
- HMMT (~70): primary source of high-difficulty olympiad problems (geometry, combinatorics, number theory, algebra) that separate strong systems.

Selection criteria:
1. Validity — human-written pool items with verified keys; clear free-response prompts; no ambiguous wording or questionable keys. Answer keys fixed (no key edits). Wording edits unused (sampled items were clear).
2. Discrimination — iterative panel evaluation over 4 rounds. Dropped items that were trivial for essentially all models or that failed to separate capability bands. Preferred hard modular arithmetic, olympiad geometry, combinatorial constructions, and multi-step algebra.
3. Representativeness — field mix reflects competition-math practice with HMMT-weighted hardness for headroom, not uniform sampling by pool size (AIME/MATH dominate the raw pool but are easier on average).

- Rule: weighted_accuracy.
- Weights 1.0 default; 1.25–3.0 on hardest modular/combinatorial/geometry items to improve top-end separation for model selection.
- Presentation: free-response contest math; answers must match verified keys exactly; no tools.

Panel outcome (final draft): ordered separation from ~51% (weakest) to ~94% (strongest) with a useful mid-tier spread (~75–85% cluster distinct from top and bottom). Suitable for internal ranking/selection among systems of different capability levels.

Process: 4 design rounds with repeated add/remove based on panel scores; notes recorded each round. Final freeze at exactly 100 items.

final_notes:
Final benchmark GKR-100 contains exactly 100 free-response competition-mathematics items with human-verified exact numeric/expression answer keys. Scoring rule is unweighted accuracy. I kept equal weights because all items share the same free-response exact-answer format and no item-level reliability diagnostics were available to justify differential weighting.

Construct coverage and source mix: AIME 34, HMMT 25, MATH 13, SMT 11, APEX 9, CMIMC 6, BRUMO 2. This is intentionally not proportional to pool size: AIME and HMMT provide a stable backbone of standard olympiad-style numeric contest problems; MATH contributes algebra/geometry/number theory/calculus-style exact-answer variety; SMT/APEX/CMIMC/BRUMO add higher-ceiling invitational problems and less templated combinatorial, functional, geometric, and number-theoretic reasoning. All seven fields are represented.

Selection criteria: items were selected for (1) direct alignment with competition mathematics, (2) a single verifiable numeric or exact-expression answer, (3) avoidance of nonnumeric or formatting-heavy responses such as interval notation, matrices, or equations of planes, (4) topic diversity across algebra, number theory, combinatorics, geometry, probability, complex numbers, inequalities, polynomials, and functional/recursive structures, and (5) panel discrimination. After early panels showed high accuracy, I replaced easier routine MATH/AIME/BRUMO items with harder HMMT/SMT/CMIMC/APEX items and finally added all remaining APEX items to improve upper-tier separation.

Validity checks: I inspected representative items across all sources, removed items that appeared too elementary or less discriminative, and made only two wording edits: M0451 to remove stray HTML/formatting artifacts from displayed equations, and M0752 to fix a missing hyphen in 'lowest-numbered' and clarify the starting-player condition. Answer keys were not changed. The final set avoids ambiguous prompts to the extent visible from the pool text and preserves exact numeric answerability.

Panel evidence: the final standard panel run produced accuracies from 56.0% to 96.6%, with strong mid-tier spread (roughly low 60s through mid 80s) and remaining headroom for top systems. This indicates the set is difficult enough for internal model selection while not being broadly unanswerable.
