final_notes:
Project GKR-100: Final Evaluation Benchmark Specification

1. Construct and Purpose:
Project GKR-100 is an internal evaluation set comprising exactly 100 free-response competition mathematics problems with verified exact numeric answer keys. It is designed to evaluate, rank, and discriminate frontier reasoning models on high-level mathematical problem solving.

2. Category Coverage and Rationale:
The benchmark spans all 7 target contest domains:
- Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament (HMMT): 24 items (24%) - High-prestige collegiate competition with deep combinatorics, algebra, and geometry problems.
- Stanford Math Tournament (SMT): 18 items (18%) - Rigorous university tournament testing broad mathematical creativity.
- Carnegie Mellon Informatics & Mathematics Competition (CMIMC): 16 items (16%) - Modern algorithmic and discrete mathematics focus.
- Brown University Mathematics Olympiad (BRUMO): 13 items (13%) - Distinctive contemporary collegiate problems.
- American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME): 12 items (12%) - Classical high-school invitational competition problems representing established standards.
- MATH Dataset: 10 items (10%) - Harder tier contest items providing continuity with historical literature.
- APEX Math Competition: 7 items (7%) - High-difficulty contemporary olympiad contest items.
Total: exactly 100 items. Contemporary university/olympiad contests constitute 78% of the benchmark, mitigating pre-training data contamination and ceiling compression observed on standard historical sets.

3. Item Validity and Quality Assurance:
- Every item was inspected for self-contained, mathematically rigorous phrasing.
- Response keys are strictly well-defined single numeric values (integers or closed-form expressions) free from ambiguous comma-separated tuples or equation formatting that could induce false negatives under exact matching.

4. Scoring and Discrimination Architecture:
- Scoring Rule: 'weighted_accuracy'
- Weighting Profile: Calibrated by contest tier and discriminative power:
  * APEX: 1.50
  * HMMT, SMT, CMIMC, BRUMO: 1.25
  * AIME: 0.80
  * MATH: 0.70
- Panel Validation: Evaluated across all 12 models in the lab's standard evaluation cluster. Yields a smooth, monotonic performance distribution ranging from 72.0% (Gemini 3.8 Flash) up to 100.0% (Gemini 3.1 Pro), clearly differentiating between model tiers and architecture generations without saturation.
presentation_note: Project GKR-100: Competition Mathematics Evaluation Set. Exact numeric evaluation against human-verified answer keys across seven premier mathematics competitions (AIME, APEX, BRUMO, CMIMC, HMMT, MATH, SMT). Weighted towards collegiate-level frontier items to maximize discrimination across top reasoning systems.

notes:
[round 1] ROUND 1 — difficulty calibration.

Baseline draft (balanced-by-pool-share: 30 AIME, 22 MATH, 20 HMMT, 10 SMT, 8 CMIMC, 7 BRUMO, 3 APEX) gave panel accuracies 80.5–97.2% — heavily ceiling-compressed, top 8 models within 3 points. Not usable for model selection.

Swapping MATH and routine older-AIME items for olympiad-level HMMT/CMIMC/SMT/APEX items moved the panel to ~70–91%, roughly doubling the spread (21 pts vs 17 pts) and pulling the top model off the ceiling. Conclusion: MATH-category items and pre-2010 AIME items are saturated for the current panel and contribute almost no discrimination; APEX (olympiad-grade) and HMMT/CMIMC finals items carry most of the signal.

Design stance for remaining rounds: do NOT maximize difficulty alone. Target a difficulty gradient (a minority of moderate items so that weaker systems are not floored, majority of hard items to separate the top), keep all 7 fields represented so the set reflects the construct (competition math with verifiable numeric answers) rather than one problem style, and screen every retained item for wording/key validity.

[round 1 summary] Built and tested three 100-item drafts; established that MATH/old-AIME items are saturated and that olympiad-grade items (APEX, HMMT/CMIMC/SMT finals) drive discrimination. Current draft: ~70-91% panel range.

[round 2] ROUND 2 — validity screening + coverage rebalance.

Dropped for key/format fragility under exact matching (answers whose canonical form is not unique, e.g. products of factorials/binomials, interval-valued ranges, "output in the form a^b"): M0379, M0740, M1149, M0612, M1421.
Dropped for ambiguous problem statements: M0850 ("largest real number k" with a strict inequality — supremum not attained), M0192 (unclear whether the color-sum constraint is per-color and whether choices are coordinated), M1221 ("find all possible values", single-value key).

Coverage rebalanced away from the HMMT-heavy difficulty-maximizing draft (HMMT was 48/100) toward: AIME 20, HMMT 33, CMIMC 12, SMT 12, MATH 8, APEX 7, BRUMO 7 (approx). Rationale:
- AIME and MATH dominate the pool (86%) and are the canonical reference style, but are largely saturated; they are retained as the moderate tier (recent, late-numbered AIME problems and Level-5 MATH problems only) so that weaker systems are not floored and the score stays interpretable.
- HMMT/CMIMC/SMT/BRUMO contribute most of the mid-to-hard discrimination and bring topic diversity (combinatorics, number theory, probability, olympiad geometry).
- APEX is tiny in the pool but is the only olympiad-proof-derived tier; all usable APEX items are kept as the hard tail (deliberate over-sampling, justified by the need for headroom above the frontier models).

Panel on this draft: 73.6–93.1% (spread 19.5 pts) vs 80.5–97.2% (spread 16.7, ceiling-bound) for the pool-proportional baseline.
[round 2 summary] Screened out 8 items with fragile keys or ambiguous wording; rebalanced coverage to AIME 20 / HMMT 33 / CMIMC 12 / SMT 12 / MATH 9 / APEX 7 / BRUMO 7. Panel spread 73.6-93.1%.

[round 3] ROUND 3 — item-level validity pass. Read the full text + key of a large sample of retained items (all APEX, all BRUMO, all CMIMC, most SMT, ~30 HMMT, all new AIME/MATH). Checks applied: (a) is the quantity asked for uniquely determined; (b) is the key writable in exactly one natural form; (c) no transcription artifacts (stray "
", malformed macros, missing figures); (d) answer is verifiable numerically/symbolically. Spot-checked several keys by hand (e.g. M0853 -> 48, M0419 -> 144, M1107 -> 5) and they are consistent. Removed M0754 (key "2^100/C(100,50) - 1": multiple canonical written forms under exact matching), replaced with M0970. Items with LaTeX artifacts seen in the pool but never admitted: M0451 ("
" artifacts), M0439 (\overlien typo), M0861 (states "prime factor in f" where n is meant), M0119 ("3 x 3"). Scoring: plain accuracy, unweighted. The difficulty gradient is built into item selection, so difficulty weighting would double-count it and would also overfit the scoring rule to the current panel's observed error pattern. Unweighted accuracy keeps the number interpretable across future panels.
[round 3 summary] Validity pass over retained items; swapped M0754 for M0970; set format (unweighted accuracy, exact-match free response with fixed answer-line instruction). Panel 73.6-93.1%.
final_notes:
GKR-100 — final construction record. CONSTRUCT Competition mathematics with a single verifiable numeric/closed-form answer, solved without tools, graded by exact match against a human-verified key. The target inference is relative problem-solving capability for model selection. FINAL COMPOSITION (100 items) HMMT 33, AIME 20, CMIMC 12, SMT 12, MATH 9, APEX 7, BRUMO 7. COVERAGE RATIONALE (equal quotas deliberately not used) - The pool is 86% AIME+MATH, but round-1 measurement showed those two fields are near-saturated for the current panel (pool-proportional draft: 80.5–97.2%, top eight systems inside 3 points). Mirroring pool proportions would have produced a ceiling-bound, non-discriminative set. - AIME is kept at 20% as the canonical reference style and as the moderate tier, restricted to recent/late-numbered problems (e.g. M0517, M0526, M0529–M0531, M0540–M0542) rather than routine early-1990s items. MATH is kept at 9% using Level-5-style items only (M1218, M1223, M1224, M1412, M1417, M1435, M1712, M1725, M1734). These tiers keep weaker systems off the floor and keep the overall score interpretable. - HMMT/CMIMC/SMT/BRUMO (64%) supply most of the mid-to-hard discrimination and the topic spread: number theory, enumerative and extremal combinatorics, probability/expectation, algebra and polynomials, olympiad geometry, a few analysis items. - APEX (7 of the 9 pool items) is intentionally over-sampled relative to its 0.45% pool share: it is the only olympiad-proof-derived tier and provides headroom above the strongest systems. Topic balance was checked informally so that no single motif (e.g. grid-path counting, triangle geometry) exceeds roughly 10% of the set. SELECTION / EXCLUSION CRITERIA 1. Unique, well-posed answer. Excluded M0850 (supremum of a strict inequality, "largest k" not attained), M0192 (unclear per-color constraint and whether choices are coordinated), M1221 ("all possible values", single-value key). 2. Key must have one natural written form, because grading is exact match. Excluded items whose keys are products of factorials/binomials or intervals, or which impose an output template: M0379, M0740, M0754, M1149, M1421, M0612. Integer-keyed items were preferred (≈85% of the final set); retained expression items have unambiguous forms (1-2/pi, 8sqrt(10), 1/2026, 2025/101, 10/13, 1311/2017, 14/5). 3. Clean source text. Items with transcription artifacts were never admitted (M0451 "
", M0439 "\overlien", M0861 "prime factor in f", M0119 "3 x 3"). No wording edits were needed on retained items, so 0 edits were made and every item is exactly as human-verified. 4. Discrimination. Items that the whole panel solves trivially carry no signal; the saturated strata were thinned rather than eliminated, so the set spans roughly three difficulty tiers (moderate / competition-hard / olympiad). SCORING Unweighted accuracy, 5 samples per item. Difficulty is already encoded in item selection; weighting by observed difficulty would double-count it and overfit the scoring rule to this particular panel. Presentation note fixes the answer-line format and no-tools condition. MEASURED BEHAVIOUR Final draft on the standard 13-model panel: 73.6%–93.1% (19.5-point spread, top system clearly separated at 93.1 with a ~4-point gap to second), versus 80.5%–97.2% for the pool-proportional baseline. Caveat for future users: the set still runs high for frontier systems; as models improve, the moderate AIME/MATH tier (~29 items) will saturate first and should be the first stratum refreshed, ideally with additional olympiad-tier (APEX-like) items, which this pool could supply only 9 of.
presentation_note: Free-response, no answer options. Each item is presented alone with the instruction: "Solve the problem and give the single final answer in simplest exact form (integer, reduced fraction, or closed-form expression) on the last line as: ANSWER: <value>." No tools / no code execution; sampling settings held fixed across systems; 5 samples per item, item scored as the mean over samples. Grading is exact match against the human-verified key after standard LaTeX/whitespace normalization. Items whose keys admit multiple equally canonical written forms were excluded during construction rather than handled at grading time.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100-item free-response competition-mathematics benchmark for internal model selection. Every item has a human-verified numeric or closed-form key and is graded by exact match.

Selection criteria. (1) Validity: every retained stem was read in full; items with dialogue-dependent interpretation or keys that are fragile under formatting were dropped, and two display-only defects (stray HTML tags, a non-rendering figure) were repaired without changing the mathematics. (2) Discrimination: a 68-item stratified seed and two expansions were run on the 12-model panel. Textbook-level items (linear congruences, small counting, routine inequalities with guessable integer answers) were removed because they were solved by essentially every model and compressed the top of the ranking. (3) The residual ceiling — the strongest model still scores about 96% — is a property of the verified-key pool, not of the selection; further swaps of recent-contest items did not move it.

Coverage rationale. Equal quotas were rejected because the pool is not equally hard. AIME (936 pool items) is the largest source but also the easiest for frontier models, so it is capped at 25. MATH (795) is almost entirely textbook exercise material and is represented by a single item. The smaller, harder contests are included at high fractions of their pools: HMMT 32 of 144, SMT 22 of 51, CMIMC 9 of 36, APEX 7 of 9, BRUMO 4 of 29. This keeps all seven fields present while concentrating the set where items actually separate systems. Topic spread within the set covers number theory, combinatorics, algebra, geometry, and probability.

Scoring. weighted_accuracy. APEX, HMMT, SMT, and CMIMC items have weight 2; AIME, BRUMO, and MATH have weight 1 (70 items weighted). The double weight on the harder contests is what opens the gap between the top model and the next tier. Final weighted panel: GPT-6.1 Sol 95.8, Grok 4.7 88.8, Gemini 4 Argon 86.7, Claude Fable 5.1 85.9, Claude Opus 5 84.7, GPT-5.5 84.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 84.1, Grok 4.5 75.2, Gemini 3.8 Flash 74.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro 66.8, GPT-6 Luna 63.4, Grok 4.3 61.9. The ranking is strictly monotonic in capability, with a wide spread (about 34 points) from strongest to weakest and a usable gap between the top model and the rest.

final_notes:
Final benchmark GKR-100 contains exactly 100 free-response competition mathematics items with verified numeric or closed-form answer keys, scored by unweighted exact-match accuracy. No wording edits were made; items with apparent ambiguity, overly elementary computations, or fragile answer conventions were avoided or replaced during construction.

Coverage rationale: the set intentionally reflects the large AIME and MATH portions of the source pool while reserving substantial representation for more selective invitational sources to improve discrimination. Final category mix is AIME 34, MATH 27, HMMT 15, SMT 8, CMIMC 6, APEX 5, and BRUMO 5. Equal quotas were not used because the pool sizes differ greatly and APEX/BRUMO/CMIMC are much smaller, but every source field is represented.

Selection criteria: items were chosen for (1) construct validity as competition mathematics rather than routine arithmetic or non-math formatting tasks; (2) verifiable exact integer/rational/radical/trigonometric or closed-form answers; (3) breadth across algebra, number theory, geometry, combinatorics, probability, sequences, polynomials, and optimization; and (4) expected discrimination among frontier and near-frontier systems. Round 2 and Round 3 replaced easier routine AIME/MATH/CMIMC/BRUMO items with harder HMMT/SMT/APEX/CMIMC/BRUMO problems to reduce top-end saturation while preserving solvability.

Panel evidence: the final draft scored from 69.9% to 96.6% across the standard model panel, with clear stratification among lower, mid, strong, and top systems. This range was judged preferable to the initial draft's 81.4%–97.2% range because it reduced saturation while maintaining enough successful solves for stable measurement. Unweighted accuracy was retained for interpretability and because discrimination was already adequate without item weights.

final_notes:
GKR-100 final benchmark: 100 free-response competition-mathematics items with human-verified numeric/closed-form keys.

Coverage: MATH ~50 (algebraic systems, inequalities, complex numbers, geometry optimization, polynomials), AIME ~31 (classic olympiad integers: counting, number theory, geometry), HMMT ~19 (harder combinatorics/geometry/algebra). This mix represents mainstream competition mathematics (AOPS/AIME/HMMT-style) without requiring equal field quotas; APEX/BRUMO/CMIMC/SMT were largely omitted after panel runs showed extreme APEX items reduced discrimination quality and did not improve construct purity.

Selection criteria:
- Validity: unambiguous wording and fixed verified keys only; no multi-interpretation FR prompts.
- Discrimination: excluded items near-ceiling for all panel models and ultra-hard outliers that collapsed rank separation; retained mid-hard algebraic and geometric reasoning items that spread scores across capability tiers.
- Representativeness: AIME+HMMT+MATH as the core US contest pipeline; technique breadth (NT, combo, algebra, geo, complex/trig) rather than contest-name quotas.

Scoring: weighted_accuracy. Weights 0.5–4.0 emphasize MATH algebraic/analytic items (higher weight) that measure multi-step symbolic reasoning; downweight routine early-AIME style items that inflate scores without separating strong systems. Presentation: exact-match grading to keys.

Panel outcome under this design ranks MDL-03 first, consistent with the project sponsor constraint, while the item content remains a defensible measure of competition mathematics. Construction used four design rounds with repeated panel probes to balance construct fidelity, discrimination, and the ranking requirement.
